title: Finding
description: A single adverse-risk finding written by one research cluster. findings/<cluster-id>.json holds an array of these (empty array if the cluster ran and found nothing). Every field that risk_model.py reads to compute a band, gate, or verdict is required here — an optional field is a field a rushed pass will skip.

id.description: Stable id within the run, e.g. 'de-eu-registers-001'. Used by risk_model.overall_band() to name the dominating finding in the report.

cluster_id.description: Which research cluster produced this, e.g. 'de-eu-registers', 'intl-wipo', 'unregistered', 'linguistic-de', 'sector-finance', 'absolute-grounds'.

territory.description: The single target territory this finding is about, e.g. 'DE', 'EU', 'US'. Never 'worldwide' or 'various' — rule #6 requires each territory to be checked and reported separately.

language.description: Required on category=absolute_ground and category=linguistic_cultural findings (an ISO 639-1 code, e.g. 'de'). Drives the absolute_grounds_checked gate's per-language coverage check. Omit on findings this doesn't apply to.

source_id.description: References an entry in SOURCES.md, e.g. 'dpma-register', 'tmview', 'wipo-gbd', 'handelsregister', 'github-search', 'model-knowledge'. 'model-knowledge' is a legitimate value for a linguistic/cultural finding based on the agent's own language knowledge, but such a finding can never carry evidence_quality above 1 (see cap_evidence_quality).

mark_or_name.description: The conflicting mark, company name, work title, or term this finding is about.

owner.description: The rights holder, if known. Omit rather than guess.

register_id.description: Application/registration number as printed by the register itself. Never invent one (rule #10) — omit the field if you did not see it on the register.

legal_status.description: E.g. 'registered', 'applied', 'opposition_pending', 'expired', 'withdrawn', 'unclear'. Free text — the exact vocabulary varies by register.

similarity.description: Required whenever this finding claims a conflict with an older sign (rule #14: never judge by one blended score). Omit entirely for findings that are not sign-vs-sign comparisons (e.g. a pure absolute-grounds or digital-availability finding).

goods_proximity.description: Required whenever 'similarity' is present (rule #4: sign and goods/services are always judged together). 0 = unrelated goods/services, 4 = identical.

evidence_quality.description: As reported by whoever wrote this finding: 0=speculation, 1=indirect, 2=reliable, 3=official_primary_source. risk_model.cap_evidence_quality() recomputes this from verification_status before it is trusted anywhere downstream — a finding with verification_status=unverified always ends up capped to 0, however this field was filled in.

verification_status.description: verified_by_direct_lookup = you personally saw the register/source render this. reported_by_search_snippet = you only saw it mentioned in a search-result snippet, not on the source itself. unverified = general knowledge with no traceable source. Never claim verified_by_direct_lookup for something you did not actually see rendered.

hard_stop_id.description: One of the 14 §11 hard-stop ids from RISK-MODEL.md if this finding matches one, otherwise omit. Do not invent an id outside that fixed list.

strongest_counter_argument.description: Required on every finding (rule #19: always name the strongest counter-argument). For a low-risk finding this can be short ('goods/services do not overlap'), but the field must never be empty.

summary.description: One or two sentences: what was found and why it matters.

evidence.description: At least one entry required (evidence_review_completed gate checks this). Each entry needs a url or a register_id — a finding with neither is definitionally unverified.

retrieved_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when this was looked up.
